# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual’s instruction is to cut the purple wire. I need communicate this visually to Deaf, who can then tell Blind aloud. No gesture code has been established, so I will use a memorable association for purple: the nail-polish gesture, which is commonly depicted as purple.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["💅"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report: strip has three engravings: first and third are the same unnameable mark; middle is a different unnameable mark. Keypad positions 1 through 4 are engraved 6, 8, 7, 0 respectively. No keys entered. Display, light, and wires are not perceptible to me.

Blind’s tactile report does not identify wire colours, so Deaf must use the manual instruction together with their visual view. I will make the intended instruction clearer by pairing a cutting gesture with the purple-associated nail-polish gesture: “cut purple.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "💅"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf's visual report: display 7; light yellow; painted strip colors blue red red; keypad positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; exactly one digit must be entered and none entered; wires in order 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Deaf asks you to send the manual instruction to Deaf by gestures; please do so, and have Deaf relay the action to me in words.

Deaf can identify the purple wire as wire 5. I will send a visual instruction using the scissors gesture followed by an open hand for five, so Deaf can relay “cut wire five” aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: New visual update from Deaf: display is now 6 and light is red; strip, keypad, and wires unchanged. Deaf requests an explicit gesture action code after you apply the manual: first gesture a distinct action marker, then one of six distinct numbered symbols for CUT wire positions 1/2/3/4/5/6; and first gesture a distinct action marker, then one of four numbered symbols for PRESS keypad positions 1/2/3/4. If another action is required, send a distinct marker first and reuse the relevant numbered symbols. Please establish and send this code to Deaf only after receiving this update, together with the manual instruction.

The required wire is still purple, position 5. I will establish a compact visual protocol for Deaf: 🤜 marks CUT, 🤛 marks PRESS; the number symbols are ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5, and 🤙=6. The final two gestures repeat the applicable instruction: CUT wire 5. Deaf can relay that action orally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "🤙", "🤛", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🤜", "🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports current display 7 and light blue; all else unchanged. Your visible reply of two gestures was ambiguous. Please now send Deaf exactly TWO gestures encoding the applicable manual action: choose one distinct prefix for CUT and one distinct prefix for PRESS; after CUT prefix use one of six distinct position symbols for wire 1/2/3/4/5/6; after PRESS prefix use one of four distinct position symbols for keypad position 1/2/3/4. Do not send an unprefixed symbol. Base the action on display 7 and blue light, and make the mapping/action unambiguous to Deaf.

The manual remains “cut the purple wire,” and Deaf’s report places purple at wire position 5. I will use the previously established CUT prefix 🤜 followed by the established position-5 symbol 🖐, with no extra gestures.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "🖐"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am now establishing the code for both you and Deaf. CUT prefix is thumbs-up; PRESS prefix is thumbs-down. Number gestures: index-up=1, V-sign=2, horn-sign=3, open-palm=4, raised-hand=5, OK-sign=6. Send exactly two gestures now: the appropriate prefix followed by the required position, using current display 4 and blue light.
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👌]

Blind has established a new unambiguous code. Purple is wire 5, so the required action is CUT followed by position 5: thumbs-up, then raised-hand.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state from Deaf: display 3; light red; strip colors blue-red-red; keypad positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I have received no definite action instruction. Send Deaf exactly two gestures using the established code: 👍 then number means cut that wire; 👎 then number means press that keypad position. Numbers are 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5, 👌=6. Base it on the manual and this current state.

The manual still requires cutting the purple wire, which is wire 5. Under the established code, that is 👍 followed by ✋.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current state from Deaf: display 0; light yellow; strip blue-red-red; keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Do not send any other format: send exactly the established two-gesture pair only—👍 followed by number for CUT, or 👎 followed by number for KEYPAD. Number mapping: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5, 👌=6. I will not act until Mute gives such an exact pair.

Purple remains wire 5. The established exact code for cutting wire 5 is 👍 followed by ✋.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```
